cohort: The study included 78 patients diagnosed with placental abruption from a total of 12599 deliveries, with maternal ages ranging from 19 to 41 years and including both primigravida and multigravida individuals.
finding: Caesarean deliveries were associated with a significantly better live birth rate compared to vaginal deliveries in cases of placental abruption.
mod_finding: Caesarean deliveries resulted in 51 live births out of 71 deliveries, demonstrating a significantly better live birth rate compared to vaginal deliveries, which yielded 3 live births out of 8 deliveries.
gest_age: Gestational age at the presentation of abruption varied from 20 to 40 weeks, with specific categories including under 27 weeks, 28-32 weeks, 33-36 weeks, and after 36 weeks.
